articles.summary: Founder of the Dvaita school of Vedanta, born at Pajaka near Udupi on the west coast of Karnataka.

sections.heading: Biography and background
sections.body: Born at Pajaka, near Udupi on the west coast of present-day Karnataka, in 13th-century India. Sources disagree on his dates: c. 1199–1278 CE in some, c. 1238–1317 CE in others; the later range is the more common.

sections.heading: Birthplace and timeline
sections.body: Birthplace: Pajaka, near Udupi. Dates are disputed (see biography). Further life events are not yet sourced.

sections.heading: Teachings and contributions
sections.body: Taught Dvaita: five fundamental distinctions (Pancha Bheda) and graded pluralism (taratamya). See Dvaita Vedanta.

sections.heading: Major works and commentaries
sections.body: Credited with 37 Dvaita texts, including thirteen commentaries on the principal Upanishads, the Brahma Sutra commentary (Madhva-bhasya), the Gita commentary (Gita-bhasya), a commentary on the Bhagavata Purana, and devotional hymns. Considered masterpiece: Anu-Vyakhyana, a supplement to the Brahma Sutra commentary. Four major works against Advaita include Upadhikhandana and Tattvadyota.

sections.heading: Disciples and lineage
sections.body: Padmanabha Tirtha headed a matha outside Tulunadu; Narahari, Madhava and Akshobhya Tirtha were meant to succeed him. Eight disciples headed the Udupi Ashta Mathas. Later lineage includes Jayatirtha and Vyasatirtha.

sections.heading: Associated places
sections.body: Pajaka (birthplace) and Udupi (Ashta Mathas). Coordinates not yet recorded.

articles.summary: Introduction to the philosophy of Dvaita Vedanta.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body: Dvaita Vedanta, also called Dvaitavada or Tattvavada, was founded by Madhvacharya.

sections.heading: Fundamental principles
sections.body: Reality contains five fundamental distinctions, each treated as real and permanent rather than provisional. Full treatment of the principles is pending.

sections.heading: Pancha Bheda (five eternal distinctions)
sections.body: Per Wikipedia: (1) between material things; (2) between matter and soul; (3) between matter and God; (4) between souls; (5) between soul and God. Other sources word this list differently; see the Pancha Bheda entry.

sections.heading: Taratamya (gradation)
sections.body: The graded nature of pluralism. Every being differs inherently from every other. These differences decide whether a soul is eligible for liberation, rebirth, or darkness, and the bliss in liberation varies with a soul's knowledge and perfection.

articles.summary: The five eternal distinctions taught in Dvaita.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Madhva taught five eternal distinctions: between material things; between matter and soul; between matter and God; between souls; and between soul and God. Each is real and permanent. Wording varies between sources.

articles.summary: The eight mathas of Udupi founded in the Madhva tradition.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Eight mathas of Udupi founded by direct disciples of Madhvacharya, each named after its village of origin: Pejavara, Palimaru, Adamaru, Puttige, Shirur, Sode, Kaniyooru and Krishnapura. They administer the Udupi Krishna temple by a rotation (paryaya); the rotation period is not yet sourced.
